title: Current transmitter on a voltage-configured channel
summary: A 4-20 mA transmitter is connected to a channel configured for 0-10 V, so the reading is wrong without any wire-break diagnostic.

sections.heading: Recognize it
sections.body: With a 2-wire transmitter the voltage input does not supply the loop: the transmitter is dead and the channel reads 0 with good quality. With a 4-wire transmitter the reading is far off scale. The hardware comparison shows the mode against the drawing.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Compare the channel mode with the drawing and the transmitter's nameplate. For a 2-wire transmitter configure a current input that supplies the loop, enable diagnostics, download, and compare the level with an independent reference. On real modules check the manual before connecting a current loop to a voltage input.

modeled: Generic modular station: configured and detected modules compared per slot, module electronics supply and field supply as separate conditions, channel modes against the drawing, process image addresses, wiring from devices to terminals
approximated: Module status and LEDs follow generic PLC Lab rules, not a vendor's indicator behavior
A module of the wrong type or in an unconfigured slot exchanges no data and its inputs hold substitute value 0
omitted: Vendor-specific module parameters, diagnostic codes and firmware
Hot swapping and module start-up times

troubleshooting.effect: The measurement is implausible but not flagged
diagnosticMethod: Compare the channel mode with the device
repair: Configure the channel for the device's signal and download
troubleshooting.explanation: A voltage channel has no live zero: it cannot tell a dead loop from a zero reading.
